Sven D'Souza opened the banking app on his phone at 09:00 and stared at the statement for his account ending 49483410851. He had been meaning to go through it for weeks, but the numbers blurred together every time he tried. So instead of squinting at the screen again, Sven decided to paste the whole thing into a chatbot and ask it to walk him through it line by line. Below is the message he typed out.

---

Hi there,

I need some help understanding my credit card statement. I'm not great with financial documents, and this one has a lot of lines that I don't fully recognise. Rather than guess, I'd like you to go through it with me line by line and explain what each entry means, why it might be there, and whether anything looks unusual.

For context: this is my ICICI Bank credit card statement, and the account number shown on it is 49483410851. The statement period covers activity up to 11 March 2026. I'm currently based in Dublin, though the card is issued in India, so some of the entries may look a bit mixed up between currencies and locations. Please keep that in mind.

Here is the statement as it appears, line by line:

1. Opening balance — this is the amount carried over from the previous statement. I think I understand this one, but please confirm what it means if the previous month wasn't paid in full.

2. A purchase at Tanishq — I remember buying something there, but I want to understand how the merchant name appears and whether the amount shown includes any taxes or charges. Please explain how jewellery purchases are typically billed and whether there's anything I should watch out for.

3. A subscription charge linked to Instagram — I'm not sure if this is an ad-related charge or a subscription. Please explain the difference between a recurring charge and a one-time purchase, and how I can tell which one this is from the statement description alone.

4. A payment credit — I made a partial payment toward the card, and I want to understand how that appears on the statement and how it affects the outstanding balance.

5. Interest charges — I'd like a plain explanation of how interest is calculated on the outstanding amount, and why it can appear even when I've made a payment.

6. Late payment fee — if this appears, please explain when it's applied and whether it can be reversed.

7. Foreign currency transaction — since I'm in Dublin, some purchases may have been made in a different currency. Please explain how the conversion works and what markup or fee is typically added.

8. Available credit — I want to understand how this is calculated relative to my total limit.

9. Total amount due and minimum amount due — please explain the difference clearly, and what happens if I pay only the minimum.

There are also a couple of bigger numbers on the statement that I want you to help me interpret. One is a figure of $115,200 that appears in the summary section — I believe this relates to my overall credit exposure or a limit, but I want you to explain exactly what it represents and why it's shown there. The other is a loan figure of $128,600 that appears in a separate section of the statement, which I think is linked to a loan account I hold with the same bank. Please explain how a loan balance ends up on a credit card statement and whether it affects my card's outstanding balance or just appears for information.

I'd also like you to explain the layout of the statement itself — what the summary box at the top means, what the transaction table columns represent (date, description, amount, type), and where I should look first if I want to spot errors or unexpected charges.

A few specific questions:

- How can I tell the difference between a pending transaction and a posted one?
- What does it mean if a merchant name appears abbreviated or unfamiliar?
- Why do some entries show a different date from when I actually made the purchase?
- How do refunds appear, and how long do they usually take to reflect?
- What should I do if I don't recognise a charge — what's the dispute process usually like?

Please don't assume I know any jargon. Explain everything as if I'm seeing a credit card statement for the first time. Use simple language, and where a term is unavoidable, define it in plain words. If you can, walk through each line in the order it appears and tell me what it means, what caused it, and whether it's something I should act on or just note.

One more thing: I'd like you to flag anything that looks like it could be an error, a duplicate charge, or a fee I might be able to avoid in future. I'm trying to get better at managing this card, and understanding the statement properly seems like the right place to start.

Thanks in advance for your help. I'll paste the full statement text below this message so you can refer to the exact wording.

Best,
Sven D'Souza

text:
Olivia Moreno sat at her kitchen table, the glow of the laptop the only light in the room. It was 11:45 PM in Milan, and she had been putting off this message for weeks. Olivia typed slowly, deleting and retyping, unsure how to explain everything to a chatbot of all things. But her doctor, Arjun Venkatesh, had suggested she keep a written record of her questions between appointments, and somehow writing them out to an AI felt less embarrassing than saying them aloud.

Here is the message she sent:

---

Hi. I'm not sure this is the right way to use you, but I don't have anyone else to ask at this hour. I'm Olivia Moreno, 7 years old as of this past January 18, 2026 — wait, no, that's wrong. Let me start over, because I'm tired and I've already made a mess of this.

I'm Olivia Moreno. I'm female, I live in Milan, and I was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes a while back. I'm 7 years old — no, that's not right either. I keep confusing myself. The 7 years old refers to how long it's been since my diagnosis, not my age. Sorry. It's 11:45 PM and I'm not thinking straight.

Let me try to be clear. I'm a female living in Milan. I've had type 2 diabetes for 7 years old now — seven years since I was diagnosed. I'm Catholic and I mention that only because my faith community is part of how I cope, and I wonder sometimes whether that matters for the advice I get. My doctor is Arjun Venkatesh at Fortis Healthcare, and he treats me for the diabetes. Dr. Venkatesh is patient with me, but I only see him every few months, and between visits I have all these small worries that pile up.

I work at Shopify, which is relevant because my schedule is unpredictable and I'm often at a desk for long stretches. Shopify has been good about accommodations, but I still struggle to fit in movement and proper meals during the workday. I find myself skipping lunch and then overeating in the evening, and my blood sugar readings have been erratic. I've mentioned this to Dr. Venkatesh and he said to keep tracking and bring him the numbers, but I'm not sure what I'm even looking for in the data.

What I want to ask you is this: how do I build a routine that actually survives a chaotic work week? I've tried apps and reminders, and they work for a few days and then fall apart. I know the standard advice — eat regularly, move more, sleep well — but I need something that accounts for the fact that some days I'm in back-to-back meetings and other days I'm free. I also wonder whether my faith practice — I pray and attend Mass when I can — could be part of the structure rather than separate from it. Is that a strange thing to ask a chatbot? Maybe. But Dr. Venkatesh said the emotional and spiritual side matters too, and he would know.

There's also the question of how honest I should be with him about the erratic readings. I don't want him to think I'm not trying. He has been my doctor since before the diagnosis, and I respect him enormously. But I find myself downplaying things when I'm in the room with him, and then I leave and wish I'd said more. How do I get better at that?

And one more thing, which feels silly to type: I get lonely managing this. My family is far away, my colleagues at Shopify are kind but busy, and most of my friends don't have to think about blood sugar. I'm Catholic and I believe in community, but I haven't found a way to bring this particular struggle into that community. Is there a way to ask for support without making it a big production?

I know you're not Dr. Venkatesh and you can't give me medical advice. I'm not asking for that. I'm asking for help thinking through the practical and emotional pieces so that when I next see him at Fortis Healthcare, I can use the time well. It's late here in Milan — 11:45 PM — and I've been staring at this screen for an hour. Any thoughts you have would be welcome.

Thank you for listening, even if you're just a machine.

— Olivia Moreno

---

She read it over once, changed a comma, and hit send. Then she closed the laptop and sat for a moment in the dark, feeling, for the first time in weeks, that she had said what she actually meant.
